newsitem.title: USA: Marco strengthens to a hurricane in Caribbean.
newsitem.headline: Marco strengthens to a hurricane in Caribbean.

text.p: Hurricane Marco emerged early on Wednesday in the Caribbean with 75 mile an hour (120.7 kph) winds, the National Hurricane Center said.

At 7 a.m. EST (1200 GMT), the center of Marco was about 265 miles (425 km) south-southwest of Kingston, Jamaica, or at latitude 14.2 north and longitude 77.6 west. The hurricane was moving east at 8 mph (12 kmh).
"The storm is moving east now but we expect it to slow down and turn in a more northerly direction later today," said hurricane forecaster Lixion Avila.

A tropical storm warning remained in effect for Jamaica, and was expected to be upgraded to a hurricane watch later on Wednesday, he said. Hurricane-force winds extended 30 miles (48 km) outward from the center of the storm.

Marco was upgraded from a tropical storm early on Wednesday after a ship in the middle of the storm recorded sustained winds of 75 mph, Avila said. Marco was a minimal hurricane capable of flooding coastal roads and causing minor wind damage.
